Holafly eSIM pricing: Is what you pay for worth it?

Table of Contents

## How much does the Holafly eSIM cost?

Holafly offers various mobile data plans, and the price you pay depends largely on your destination and the duration of your plan. The standout feature of the service is that most Holafly plans offer unlimited data, and because of that, they usually come at a higher price compared to competitors.

Let’s take Holafly’s unlimited data plans for one day as a reference. The starting price is US$3.90 per day, and afterward the price varies quite a bit depending on your destination and plan type:

City plans cost up to US$9.90 per day.

Single-country plans cost up to US$11.90 per day.

Regional plans cost up to US$15.90 per day for multi-country coverage. [...] ### Is a Holafly eSIM really unlimited?

Yes, Holafly provides unlimited data for the majority of its plans, but there are a few catches. If you use an excessive amount of data in a single day, local carriers may throttle your speeds and make your connection sluggish. Holafly also caps hotspot tethering at 500MB to 1 GB per day. So while technically you have unlimited data, these restrictions mean you might not always get to use it to its full potential.

### What is Holafly eSIM pricing in Europe?

Holafly offers unlimited data plans for both individual European countries and the region as a whole. Its regional eSIM for Europe covers 33 countries, and the price ranges from US$3.90 for a single day to US$74.90 for 30 days. You can choose the exact number of days you need for your trip. [...] ## What affects Holafly eSIM pricing?

Because Holafly focuses on unlimited data, it’s one of the more expensive eSIM options on the market. You pay for the convenience of not tracking how much data you use. But that peace of mind comes with a higher starting price than competitors with smaller, fixed-data packages can offer.

Aside from the unlimited data, the three other factors that affect Holafly plan prices are:

Destination. Your destination plays a massive role in pricing. Like many other eSIM providers, Holafly relies on local carriers to provide your connection. Because carrier fees and the general cost of internet connection vary by country, these differences are reflected in the price you pay for your eSIM.

results.title: Airalo eSIM: Guide to Staying Connected on the Go - LoungePair
results.content:
### Does an Airalo eSIM come with a number?

When it comes to eSIM numbers, some Airalo plans come with a number, but others don’t. We understand that the company is working to add more options over time. Make sure to check the description of your chosen eSIM for information on whether it comes with a number, especially if this is a must for you when travelling.

### How much does Airalo cost?

Airalo's eSIMs start from US$4.50 for 1GB of data. This makes it an affordable and convenient option for travellers looking for a flexible, cost-effective way to stay connected while on the go. Costs differ depending on the region or country you intend to purchase an eSIM for, so we recommend just downloading their app and checking the current pricing for your destination.

## Summing Up [...] The availability of eSIMs and coverage can vary by region and country, so it is recommended that users check the list of covered countries on the Airalo website before purchase (particularly for the regional and global eSIM) to confirm availability for their destination.

Most popular countries listed on the Airalo website including the USA, Canada, New Zealand and Australia

Most popular countries listed on the Airalo website including the USA, Canada, New Zealand and Australia

## Customer service and support

When it comes to support, Airalo has several options available to help users with their eSIM data plan. [...] Local eSIMs allow users to get coverage in one of the 190+ countries that Airalo covers. This is a good choice if you're only visiting one country on your trip.

Regional eSIMs give coverage for entire regions and continents. For example, the Eurolink regional eSIM covers 39 countries in Europe, and The Island Hopper regional eSIM covers 24 Caribbean islands. There are also regional eSIMs for Africa, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia. This eSIM is a great option if you're on a multi-country trip within the same region.

Global eSIMs give coverage for 87 countries, ranging from 1-20 GB and 7-180 days of validity. If you're planning a multi-country trip in multiple regions of the world, this is the eSIM for you.

searchResult.answer: Nomad eSIM offers 50 GB plans for 30 days in various countries, starting from $27 in the US and ranging up to $45 in India. Prices vary significantly by region and data amount. Nomad's US pricing is $4.50 for 1GB for seven days.

results.title: Nomad eSIM - Review 2024 - PCMag Middle East
results.content:
(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] (Credit: Iyaz Akhtar)

You can view your data usage in the Manage tab of the Nomad app, where you can also see details like when your plan will expire and buy more data. If your data is running low or is set to expire, you will receive a notification. You can purchase additional data at the same price as regular plans. For example, an additional 1GB costs $4.50.

## Final Thoughts

results.content:
Pricing & Value: When comparing costs, look at the price per day or per gigabyte. Local eSIMs are significantly cheaper than international roaming. Watch out for any hidden fees, as most reputable eSIM services are prepaid with no extra charges. A good value plan might cost around $2–$3 per day for unlimited data.

 Ease of Setup & Use: A key benefit of eSIMs is their simplicity. Look for providers that offer instant delivery of a QR code and clear, simple activation instructions. The best services allow you to purchase ahead of time and activate the plan upon arrival, ensuring you don’t lose any days of service. [...] Japan Wireless Team

Japan’s tourism is booming again in 2025 – and eSIMs have become the go-to solution for travelers to stay connected. This guide compares top local eSIM providers (Japan Wireless, NipponSim, eSIM Japan) to help you choose the best unlimited data plan for your trip.

Japan has seen a surge in tourists since reopening – 36.9 million foreign visitors came in 2024, a record high (up 47% from 2023). In the first half of 2025 alone, over 21.5 million travelers visited Japan (on pace to exceed 40 million for the year). Major events like the Expo 2025 in Osaka (expected to draw ~28 million attendees) are further boosting inbound travel. With so many tourists, staying connected is essential – and more visitors are turning to eSIMs as the easiest way to get online in Japan. [...] Short Trips (Up to 1 Week): If you’re visiting Japan for only a few days or a week, you likely won’t need tons of data, but convenience is key. An unlimited plan for the week ensures you won’t have to ration data. Japan Wireless’s 7-day Unlimited eSIM is a top choice – it provides full speed data each day and easy setup, so you’re covered for your whole stay. For comparison, some global eSIM providers like Airalo offer 5–10 GB one-week plans, but those have data limits and sometimes lower speeds. With a local unlimited eSIM, you can freely use maps, upload Instagram stories, and video chat without worrying about running out. The cost difference is minor (e.g. ~$30 for 7-day unlimited vs ~$20 for a 5 GB plan), and the extra peace of mind is worth it.

results.title: Buying a SIM Card or eSIM for Travel in Taiwan (2026 Guide)
results.content:
Luckily all of the main companies have booths at Taoyuan airport, so you’ll be able to compare prices at a glance. After you’ve cleared immigration and collected your bags, walk out into the arrivals hall and turn right. Follow the signs for the buses — just before you get to the end of the arrival hall and escalators to take you down to where the buses leave from, you’ll see several booths on your right.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

Hello, [...] ## Travel eSIM for Taiwan

Compared to buying locally, it’s cheaper to get a travel eSIM unless you really need unlimited amounts of data for your stay. That’s the option I’ve suggested to friends who’ve visited Taiwan in the last couple of years, and they’ve all come back happy with the speeds, service, and (especially) cost.

Nomad typically has the lowest prices, around ten bucks for 10GB of data, with smaller and larger options available. If you don’t need much data, take a look at Instabridge as well: its smaller bundles can be very cheap.

Prices and packages change regularly, of course, so check the table below before making a final decision. The details were last updated on 9 Mar 2026.

## Travel eSIM for Taiwan

Compared to buying locally, it’s cheaper to get a travel eSIM unless you really need unlimited amounts of data for your stay. That’s the option I’ve suggested to friends who’ve visited Taiwan in the last couple of years, and they’ve all come back happy with the speeds, service, and (especially) cost.

Nomad typically has the lowest prices, around ten bucks for 10GB of data, with smaller and larger options available. If you don’t need much data, take a look at Instabridge as well: its smaller bundles can be very cheap.

Prices and packages change regularly, of course, so check the table below before making a final decision. The details were last updated on 9 Mar 2026.

Airalo
Airalo [...] Luckily all of the main companies have booths at Taoyuan airport, so you’ll be able to compare prices at a glance. After you’ve cleared immigration and collected your bags, walk out into the arrivals hall and turn right. Follow the signs for the buses — just before you get to the end of the arrival hall and escalators to take you down to where the buses leave from, you’ll see several booths on your right.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

Hello, [...] Like most travel eSIMs, these are data-only: you don’t get a local number. I use apps for everything from communication to transport these days, so the lack of a local number very rarely matters to me, but you might have different needs.

If you’re new to eSIMs, they offer big benefits to travelers in terms of how quickly, easily, and (often) cheaply you can get connected when you arrive in a new country. Most recent phones support them.

Going to other countries as well? Be sure to check out my quick and easy eSIM finder with real-world recommendations for every trip: it only takes a few seconds, and could save you a ton of money!

Traveltomtom recommends ordering an eSIM for traveling in Hong Kong from one of the well-known eSIM providers that have proven to be reliable eSIM operators: Jetpac, Holafly, SimOptions, Nomad, Airalo, GigSky, Airhub, aloSIM, Saily, Roamless, Firsty, Yesim, Sim Local, Ubigi, etc.

The competition is fierce nowadays... so before you buy an eSIM first read my tips below!

### SimOptions

SimOptions is a very reliable eSIM provider and Traveltomtom has used SimOptions uncountable times in more than 50 countries around the world. I can totally recommend using SimOptions for ordering an eSIM.

SimOptions is always one of Traveltomtom's top recommendations read our honest SimOptions review for more info about this eSIM provider. [...] The cheapest tourist sim cards start around $10 USD and up. You can buy them in the official retail stores of in the city center of every popular tourist destination in Hong Kong, but also in convenience stores. But for $10 USD you get calling minutes and 7 GB data included for use in Hong Kong. There are also prepaid sim card deals for around $12 USD that give you 12 GB data.

Keep in mind when buying a sim card in a convenience store you will have to do the passport registration manually. A bit of a hassle and you have to wait for verification. [...] Truely eSIM Review: Unlimited Travel eSIM tested
